michigan.watch: Oakland, Macomb and Wayne counties, where Stevens led the primary, against comparable places where she did not.

maine.title: Maine Senate
maine.watch: Collins’s margin against the Republican candidate for governor, town by town.

texas.title: Texas Senate
texas.watch: Paxton’s margin against Abbott’s, county by county.

pennsylvania.title: Pennsylvania House
pennsylvania.watch: Whether the four districts swing by similar amounts.

alaska.title: Alaska Senate
alaska.watch: Daniel J. Sullivan’s first-choice share compared with his 2.5% in the primary.

redistricting.title: Redistricting 2026
redistricting.watch: Texas and Florida seats drawn on 2024 margins: do they hold in a less favorable environment?

reach.title: The wave’s reach
reach.watch: The gap between each Senate margin and Trump’s 2024 margin.
reach.any: sherrod brown|jon husted|ashley hinson|josh turek|roger marshall|adam hamilton|darline graham|annie andrews|kansas senate|iowa senate|ohio senate|south carolina senate

massachusetts.title: Massachusetts ballot questions
massachusetts.watch: Whether Question 7 passes, and in which kinds of towns.

midterm-penalty.name: Midterm penalty
midterm-penalty.why: The president’s party usually loses House seats in midterms.
midterm-penalty.watch: Net House seat change, the national House vote, and whether losses concentrate in seats the president’s party won narrowly in 2024.

referendum.name: Referendum and retrospective voting
referendum.why: Voters reward or punish the party in power for conditions they experience.
referendum.watch: Whether vote choice tracks evaluations of the economy and the Iran war in exit polls and AP VoteCast, and whether places more exposed to fuel prices move differently.

veto-players.name: Divided government and veto players
veto-players.why: Each actor whose agreement is required makes policy change harder.
veto-players.watch: Chamber control, committee gavels, confirmations and the next appropriations fight.

nationalization.name: Nationalization
nationalization.why: Local races increasingly move together with national party forces.
nationalization.watch: Whether districts with different demographics and incumbents swing by similar amounts.

turnout.name: Turnout versus persuasion
turnout.why: Margins change when voters switch, or when a different electorate shows up.
turnout.watch: Turnout by county relative to 2022 and 2024; later, validated voter files.

realignment.name: Realignment versus short-term swing
realignment.why: Durable coalition change is not the same as one unusual election.
realignment.watch: Whether the 2024 shift among Hispanic voters in Texas persists, reverses or deepens, office by office.

elite-cues.name: Elite cues and endorsements
elite-cues.why: Trusted figures help voters infer which choice fits their values.
elite-cues.watch: Movement among the sender’s constituency after the cue, relative to comparable places or people.

incumbency.name: Incumbency and the personal vote
incumbency.why: Officeholders can build support that outlasts party tides.
incumbency.watch: Incumbents’ margins relative to their party’s baseline on the same ballot.

candidate-quality.name: Candidate quality
candidate-quality.why: Experienced, scandal-free candidates tend to beat what partisanship predicts.
candidate-quality.watch: Performance relative to co-partisans on the same ballot.

party-coalitions.name: Party coalitions, primaries and nominations
party-coalitions.why: Nominations reveal bargaining among a party’s factions.
party-coalitions.watch: Whether primary losers’ supporters return in November, and how replacement nominees perform.

campaign-finance.name: Campaign finance and outside spending
campaign-finance.why: Money buys communication and organization, but it follows competitiveness.
campaign-finance.watch: Who spends, when, and on what; differences across media markets.

redistricting.name: Gerrymandering and the seats–votes link
redistricting.why: District lines translate votes into seats, and interested actors draw them.
redistricting.watch: Seat outcomes compared with notional baselines on the new lines.

electoral-rules.name: Electoral rules and ballot design
electoral-rules.why: Ranked ballots, primary systems and ballot layout shape incentives and outcomes.
electoral-rules.watch: First choices, transfers, exhausted ballots and undervotes.

federalism.name: Federalism and election administration
federalism.why: States run elections; federal actors and courts contest the edges.
federalism.watch: Litigation over ballots and certification (California, Alaska) and court rulings on maps.

direct-democracy.name: Direct democracy and policy design
direct-democracy.why: When voters legislate, drafting and implementation become the policy.
direct-democracy.watch: Implementation guidance, local responses and measurable outcomes after passage.

ecological-inference.name: Ecological inference
ecological-inference.why: Aggregate patterns do not reveal individual behavior.
ecological-inference.watch: Precinct shifts together with surveys or validated voter files.

ticket-splitting.name: Ticket splitting and same-ballot comparison
ticket-splitting.why: Same voters, same day, different choices: the cleanest comparison in election data.
ticket-splitting.watch: Senate versus governor margins in the same counties: Maine, Texas, Michigan, Pennsylvania.
